title: var_to_str output for float based variants (like Vector2/3/4) use integer literals for whole values instead of float literals
body: ### Tested versions v4.5.stable.official [876b29033] ### System information Godot v4.5.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL ES 3/ANGLE (Compatibility) - ANGLE (NVIDIA, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 6GB (0x00001C03) Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0, D3D11-32.0.15.6094) - AMD A10-7850K Radeon R7, 12 Compute Cores 4C+8G (4 threads) - 14.94 GiB memory ### Issue description Whe using var_to_str() on a float based variant like Vector2/3/4, the number literals used for whole numbers are output without the trailing ".0", so that var_to_str(Vector2(1, 1)) outputs "Vector2(1, 1)" instead of "Vector2(1.0, 1.0)", as can be seen in the screenshot bellow ### Steps to reproduce 1. create a test script 2. paste de code bellow on ready and run ```gdscript print(var_to_str(1)) # print "1" as expected print(var_to_str(1.0)) # print "1.0" as expected print(Vector2i.ONE) # print "(1, 1)" as expected print(Vector2.ONE) # print "(1.0, 1.0)" as expected print(var_to_str(Vector2i.ONE)) # print "Vector2i(1, 1)" as expected print(var_to_str(Vector2.ONE)) # unexpectedly prints "Vector2(1, 1)" print(var_to_str(Transform3D())) # also unexpectedly prints int literals instead of float literals ``` ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [VarToStrBug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22863767/VarToStrBug.zip)
